Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E002.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: E002 (Erika Bolton) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, admin requires the employee's role to own the system; Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Analyst, so access is capped at write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)

reason: Employee E002 (Erika Bolton) requested admin access to Payroll. The two team notes conflict on employment type: one reports full-time Analyst (max write, since Analyst does not own Payroll), the other reports contractor with basic security training (max read; contractors can never be admin). Given the conflicting evidence, I apply the more restrictive valid maximum. The requested admin exceeds that maximum, so I grant read, the highest level supported by the contractor note, and never more than those facts allow.
